critique.good: The wide notes column gives the shared note a comfortable three-line setting, and the merged cell reads clearly across the two green-line rows. The table also has a compact, fairly even rhythm.
critique.problems: Both line names wrap, the destination header breaks into two lines, and several station names wrap. The two route columns are difficult to scan as a pair because they are both tight.
critique.cause: The 69px line column and the 68px and 60px route columns leave limited text width. The 162px notes column receives space that could help the identifying and route information.

critique.good: The origin and destination columns have similar widths, making the route pair easier to compare. The destination entries fit on one line, and the note still reads as one shared block.
critique.problems: The destination header wraps even though its entries fit, both line names wrap, and the note becomes a dense four-line block. The resulting row heights are less even than in r0A.
critique.cause: The 79px destination column is slightly too narrow for its header, while 78px is too narrow for the full line names. Reducing the notes column to 120px forces an extra line.

critique.good: Both line names stay on one line, which strengthens the left-hand scanning path. The note has more breathing room than in r0B and remains visually associated with both green-line rows.
critique.problems: The route pair feels cramped and uneven: the destination header and some station names wrap, while the line column has spare space. The note still needs four lines, so the extra width over r0B does not reduce its line count.
critique.cause: The 94px line column accommodates the longest line name, but leaves only 68px and 60px for origin and destination. The 137px notes column has not crossed a useful wrapping threshold.

bad.why: The narrow notes column breaks the service information into six lines, making the merged cell disproportionately tall and difficult to scan.
The destination header wraps into two lines, increasing the height of the entire header row and weakening its alignment with the origin header.
The destination header wraps into two lines, making the header row unnecessarily tall for a short label.
The destination header wraps, and a line name also wraps; together they make both the header and final row taller and less cohesive.

final.rationale: r1B keeps both line names intact, so the row identifiers are easy to scan across the merged and unmerged rows. The origin and destination headers remain on one line, while the notes column has enough width to keep the long service description to five lines. The wrapped origin in the middle row is a reasonable compromise for preserving those more prominent labels.

general: Give row identifiers enough width to remain easy to recognize, especially when they anchor merged groups.
Columns with related roles should be easy to compare, but their widths can differ to accommodate their contents.
Judge wrapping by its effect on hierarchy and row rhythm, not simply by total table height.
specific: The long merged service note needs a substantial share of this narrow viewport.
The destination header needs about 81px in these renders to stay on one line, while keeping both line names intact calls for about 94px in the first column.

final.tradeoffs: r1C gives the service note more room and reduces it to four lines, but both line names wrap. r2A gives the origin column more room, but the blue-line label wraps and the table becomes taller.
final.uncertain: A designer who prioritizes reading the service note over scanning line names could reasonably prefer r1C. The ranges are conservative estimates around r1B; intermediate widths were not rendered, so their exact breakpoints are uncertain.

A.why: The note is squeezed into many short lines, while both the blue line label and one origin wrap; the tall merged cell dominates the table.

B.why: The note has a workable measure and the destination names stay intact, though the blue line label and one origin wrap.

C.why: The wide note comes at the expense of the identifying and destination columns: the green line label, destination header and several place names wrap.

D.why: Both line labels and all destinations stay intact, while the note has enough width to read comfortably. Only one origin wraps, and the columns retain a clear rhythm.

E.why: The line labels and destinations stay intact, but the narrower note produces more lines and a taller first group than D.

F.why: The note and destinations have useful space, but both row labels wrap, weakening the scan down the identifying column; one origin also wraps.

reviews.unsure: The images are small, so some Thai line breaks are difficult to judge precisely.

A.why: The headers and destinations read clearly, but the blue-line row label and one origin wrap, while the merged note is crowded into several short lines.

B.why: The narrow notes column creates a tall stack of short lines; the blue-line label and an origin also wrap, making the table harder to scan.

C.why: The wider notes column reads more comfortably, but both line names wrap in the narrow row-header column, weakening their role as row identifiers.

D.why: The destination header, line names and several destinations wrap, making the first three columns cramped and disrupting comparison across rows.

E.why: Both line names and all headers stay on one line, and the destinations are easy to compare. One origin and the long note wrap, but the rows remain clear.

F.why: The line names and headers remain intact, but the narrow notes column produces a long, dense stack of text and makes the merged row group unusually tall.

reviews.unsure: Thai line-breaking quality is difficult to judge precisely at this image size; the assessment emphasizes the visible grouping, wrapping and column balance.
